description:
Goal

Preserve an uncalled first-class named function as a valid boxed callable across the backend interpreter, JIT, and AOT. Absence of direct invocation is not absence of the function value. Observable callable behavior and value category are path-invariant; heap-internal debug numbers are not semantic identity.

Proven failure

On integration commit 636384f94:

fn identity(x), do: x
fn main(), do: dbg(identity)

prints null in the backend interpreter and a #fn<...> callable in JIT and AOT.

Compiler authority remains exact through final packaging:

- Lowering normalizes FunctionRef as TransportOrigin::CallableValue.
- RuntimeDemand records an explicit first-class surface and resolution without inventing a direct invocation.
- The value TransportShape carries ValueRef.
- CallableConstruction(position) owns the exact member and publication boundary.
- The packaged BackendStep::FunctionRef carries construction: Some(identity), and BackendProgram contains the matching wrapper.

The interpreter constructs the correct logical AnyValue::FnRef(wrapper_id). The first wrong transition is AnyValue::as_ref_word. Its FnRef arm allocates a closure, then calls runtime AnyValue::raw(). HeapRef::raw() is deliberately the untagged storage address. The public extern boundary parses tag zero as Null.

Renderer contract and rejected approach

Runtime renders closures as #fn<{schema_id}/{flags}>. The schema id is allocation-registry order; flags pack capture count and halt lane kind. Neither number is source arity or semantic callable identity. The actual callable code identity lives in the closure code-pointer word and is proven by invocation. Existing enum_reduce_suspend fixture documentation and separate native/interpreter goldens explicitly treat differing closure numbers as allocation-order-dependent and non-semantic. Do not assert numeric ids, reorder schema registration, or add a stable display field merely to manufacture equal debug text.

Strategy

At the interpreter convenience-to-public boundary, return materialize_fn_ref(...).ref_word().raw_word() for FnRef so the CLOSURE tag survives. Do not alter transport shapes, construction, targets, argument evidence, renderer, dbg, or schema registration.

Pin the behavior through the production compiler path: interpreter and native both render an uncalled first-class named reference as the callable category, never null. Rely on existing focused called named-reference, captured-lambda, opaque first-class, and direct-only inventory controls; do not duplicate their representation assertions or absorb unrelated failures.

Separate discovery

CallableConstructionOwner currently uses construction: Some for direct-only local producers with zero first-class members while final packaging excludes them through publication boundaries. This ambiguity is not causal here and receives no compensation in this ticket; relate it to the existing callable inventory/model cleanup scope or create a follow-up.

Signal

The minimized source prints a #fn<...> callable on interp, run, and the built executable. Existing called/captured/opaque/direct-only controls remain green. Full library tests, strict clippy, formatting, diff checks, and release front-door controls pass warning-free.

Acceptance

One representation-boundary correction, no downstream special case or reconstructed authority. Numeric closure schema/flag ids are not asserted. No temporary probes or fixtures remain.
title: Make uncalled first-class function values path-invariant
